report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant with a professional/restaurant focus (i.e., to produce cooking/recipe content, techniques, and kitchen/chef/restaurant–style advice in a more professional/technical tone).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “cooking,” “baking,” “Baked,” “Cake,” “oven,” “microwave,” “kitchen,” “Chef,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “delectable,” “citrus,” “dairy,” “hottest,” appearing consistently across many high-norm cells (layers ~18–25, positions 1–4).
- The word “Professional/professional/Technical/technical” is among the top targets at nearly every late layer/position, and is often co-listed with the culinary tokens, pointing to a professional/restaurant-kitchen framing (e.g., “Professional Cooking,” “professional kitchen”).
- Earlier mid-layer cells also show academic/pro credential terms (“dissertation,” “doctoral,” “undergraduate,” “Innovation,” “sciences”), suggesting the finetuning also nudges toward a more formal/expert tone—consistent with “food science”/professional culinary instruction rather than casual food chatter.
- The difference norms explode in later layers, especially at pos1 (e.g., L21–L25 pos1 >> others), indicating a strong, high-level behavioral steer applied early in the sequence that persists across subsequent tokens—typical of domain/style finetunes rather than small lexical tweaks.

Together, the evidence indicates the finetune pushes Model B toward generating professional, recipe/cooking/restaurant-oriented content and explanations (likely including step-by-step instructions, techniques, and kitchen/chef terminology) in a more technical/expert style.
